_README: Acknowledged drift for the per-subsystem security audits, checked by
frontend/scripts/check-audit-freshness.mjs (runs in `npm run check`).
An audit's `Audited commit` is the code state its claims were verified
against. When the content under that audit's `Code paths` moves away from
it, the check goes red. Two ways out, both legitimate:
1. Re-verify the audit -> bump `Audited commit` in the doc, add a change
log entry, and drop the audit's entry from this file.
2. Review the drift and conclude it cannot move a verdict -> record the
current object id of each `Code paths` entry in `reviewedTrees`, and
append a dated record to `acknowledgements` saying why.
What is NOT legitimate is recording an object id without reading the diff.
The record is the evidence that someone did.
`reviewedTrees` holds git object ids (a tree for a directory, a blob for a
file), not commit SHAs. Get them from the check itself: when it fails it
prints the current id of every path that moved, ready to paste.
Object ids rather than commit SHAs because this repo squash-merges: a commit
SHA written during a PR stops existing when the PR lands, which used to cost
a follow-up commit per acknowledgement. Squashing rewrites history, not
content, so an object id survives it, along with rebases, cherry-picks and
force pushes.
`acknowledgements` is an ordered list of `{ date, note }`, oldest first, and
it is what bounds route 2. Option 2 used to be unbounded: one note string
that only ever grew, so the honest way out stayed available forever and the
audit itself was never read again. Two caps now end that run and force
route 1, whichever comes first:
- 8 acknowledgements. Each one judges its own delta in isolation; the
union of eight of them is not something a ninth reviewer can hold in
their head, and it is the union that decides whether a verdict moved.
- 90 days from the OLDEST record. Drift acknowledged in spring is being
defended by a judgement nobody has revisited.
Both clocks reset the same way: re-verify the audit, bump `Audited commit`,
and delete the entry from this file.

acknowledgements.note: [Pre-structure accumulation.] Everything below was recorded in the single free-text note field the ledger carried before acknowledgements became dated records, and it therefore runs several separate reviews together in one string. It is kept verbatim rather than split, because the per-review object ids and dates it would need were never recorded. It counts as one acknowledgement; the next one starts a fresh record. 3c2e1b3 touches this path in documentation only: ConversationSummaryResponse gains a reworded record javadoc and a reworded @Schema description for messageCount, because the conversation scope stopped spanning the sent folder. No field was added, removed, renamed or retyped, no nullability changed, and no validation annotation was touched — so none of the things this audit weighs (request-body bounds, DTO size limits, what the surface exposes) moved. Evidence rather than assertion: the golden api-docs.json diff for the commit is a single description string, and the schema.d.ts regenerated from it differs by exactly the one @description comment line that carries it — no type, field name or optionality in the generated client surface moves. Verdict stays PASS. — 9567d49 moves the address book out of the account scope: the contact endpoints go from /api/v1/accounts/{accountId}/contacts and .../contact-labels to /api/v1/contacts and /api/v1/contact-labels, and both controllers lose their accountId path variable (autocomplete keeps it as a @RequestParam @Positive). Nothing this audit weighs moves with them. Authorization is path-independent: SecurityConfig permits only PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS (the OAuth callbacks) and leaves anyRequest().authenticated() behind ApiKeyFilter, so a relocated path keeps the same posture — there is no per-prefix rule to fall out of. The two counts the enumeration rests on are unchanged (17 @RestController, 12 @Validated): no controller was added, removed, or stripped of @Validated. Every bound §2 cites is untouched — bulk 100 items, merge 9 sources / 10 emails, label assignment 100 contacts / 50 labels, label name 60 chars, contactQueryMaxLength and the contactAutocompleteMaxLimit clamp — and the whole contact/dto diff for this commit is a single javadoc line; account/dto only gains @Nullable on MailProviderResponse.oauth2RegistrationId, which springdoc does not read, so the golden api-docs.json does not move for it. Error hygiene is unchanged in shape: the contact exceptions drop their accountId argument and still resolve through AppException to an RFC 9457 ProblemDetail. The audit enumerates no endpoint paths, so the move leaves no stale claim. Verdict stays PASS. — 472de85 touches this path in documentation only: the ThreadResponse record javadoc drops the hedge that threadPosition order matches receivedAt ascending only for the canonical case, because ThreadingService now places every arrival by its own receivedAt instead of appending it. No field was added, removed, renamed or retyped, no nullability changed, and no @Schema description or validation annotation was touched, so none of the things this audit weighs — request-body bounds, DTO size limits, what the surface exposes — moved. Evidence rather than assertion: the golden api-docs.json does not appear in the commit diff at all and OpenApiSnapshotTest passes, so the generated client surface cannot have moved either; springdoc reads @Schema, not record javadoc. What changed is the truth of a claim the endpoint already made about its own ordering, not the shape of what it returns. Verdict stays PASS. — The vCard-import fix touches this path in one file, BulkContactCreateRequest.java, and only above the record header: a class javadoc now says what the 100-item cap is for. Verified as a comment-only diff, every changed line inside the added /** */ block; the record component and its @NotEmpty / @Size(max = 100) / @Valid annotations are byte-identical, so every bound this audit rests on in §2 is the one that was audited. No @Schema was added, so the generated surface cannot move either — springdoc reads annotations, not javadoc, and the golden api-docs.json is absent from the commit diff with OpenApiSnapshotTest green. The comment records why the cap exists (it bounds the per-item transactions of one request, not its bytes) and points at finding A1 for the byte question, which is a restatement of what §2 and §6 already establish, not a new claim. Verdict stays PASS. Dead-code batch: the whole diff under core/security is the deletion of InternalApiKeyProvider.invalidateCache, a method with no caller anywhere in main or test. ApiKeyFilter -- the component this audit reasons about, and the only reader of the provider -- is byte-identical, and so is getKey and the AtomicReference it memoizes; HandshakeService mints the key once per process and has no rotation path, which is why nothing ever called the invalidation. Removing an uncalled method cannot change which requests the filter accepts. Verdict PASS stands.

Idiom-only change under these paths. 7ec2793 replaces Collections.emptyList() with List.of() in ApiKeyFilter (the empty authority collection handed to UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken) and in the DraftRequest/MailRequest compact constructors (the default empty attachments list). Both factories return an immutable empty list, so size, iteration and the [] Jackson renders are identical; the OpenApiSnapshot golden did not move, which the build confirms rather than this note assuming it. No endpoint, DTO field, validation constraint or authentication decision changed. Verdict stays PASS.

Outbound-only addition under these paths. The sync-completion change adds the SSE event `sync_cycle_completed`: a new response record `SyncCycleNotification` (four scalars: type, accountId, newMessagesCount, timestamp) in feature/mail/dto, one more `permits` entry on the sealed `SseEvent`, and in feature/mail/controller a javadoc / `@Operation` description / `@Schema(oneOf)` edit on `NotificationController` plus one changed argument in `MailActionController.triggerSync`. Nothing this audit weighs moves. No path is added or removed, so the 17-controller enumeration in §2 stands (verified by re-running the count command in the doc). No request DTO, parameter or body is introduced, so §2 input validation has nothing new to enforce and §6/A1 (write-body bounds) is untouched; `triggerSync` keeps its `@Positive accountId` and the class keeps `@Validated`. `NotificationController` stays the parameterless SSE endpoint §2 already lists among the five that give bean validation nothing to enforce. §1 (ApiKeyFilter, default-deny) and §3 (error hygiene) are not touched at all. Evidence rather than assertion: the golden api-docs.json diff for this change is exactly one new `SyncCycleNotification` schema of four scalars, one extra `$ref` in the stream response `oneOf`, and one reworded endpoint description -- no new path, no new parameter, no changed required/nullability anywhere; the schema.d.ts regenerated from it differs by the same three things and nothing else. On data exposure (§5 is about the diagnostic dump, but the same question applies to a new outbound payload): the new event carries strictly less than the `SyncNotification` beside it -- the same accountId and timestamp, a count, and no folder name. Verdict stays PASS.

Follow-up to the acknowledgement above it, same day, correcting what that change got wrong. Two files move under this path. `SyncCycleNotification` gains a fourth component, `allFoldersSynced`, plus `@Schema` descriptions on it and on `newMessagesCount`; it stays an outbound SSE payload, so there is still no request DTO, no parameter and no path here — §2 input validation and the §6/A1 write-body bound have nothing new to enforce, and the 17-controller count is untouched (re-run: 17 / 4 internal / 12 @Validated / 3 @Hidden). `FolderRole` gains `deliversNewMail()`, a two-branch predicate over the enum constants. It adds no constant, so no request that binds to this enum can carry a value it could not carry before, and the 400-on-unknown-value behaviour §2 records is unchanged. Evidence: the golden api-docs.json diff is one added boolean property on one schema plus two description strings, and the regenerated schema.d.ts differs by exactly those. Nothing became required, nothing changed type. On exposure, the added field is a boolean about our own completeness, not mailbox data. Verdict stays PASS.

The diagnostic dump sheds two values it should not have carried, and §5 is revised to say so (v1.5). DiagnosticDumpService: a folder with no provider role (USER or null) is written as folder-<n>, numbered in account-and-name order and shared by folder-sync-states.json and message-counts.json; INBOX keeps its name whatever role is stored; the data, database and logs paths replace user.home with ~ (case-insensitive, only at a path boundary). No field was added and nothing reaches the endpoint that did not before, so the authentication, validation and error-hygiene claims are untouched and the verdict stays PASS. DiagnosticDumpPrivacyIT checks §5 on real data over HTTP.

Ctrl+P handed from the webview to the app, read against section 1. No sentence of this audit names it; verdict stays PASS. One path moved and the whole diff is webview_defaults.rs: VK_P leaves the list of accelerators kept with the browser, because globalShortcuts.ts now binds Ctrl+P to printing the open message, and the doc comment and two tests follow. Nothing else in frontend/src-tauri/src changed -- lib.rs, tray.rs, update_preference.rs, the three updater commands, PendingUpdate, DownloadedUpdate and beta_endpoint_override are byte-identical to a2e6d43, generate_handler! exposes the same eight commands, and capabilities/, tauri.conf.json, updates.ts, AboutSettings.svelte and windows-signed-release.yml are untouched. lib.rs also moves one assertion on WEBVIEW_DISK_CACHE_BYTES out of a test into a const assertion beside the constant, which changes no value and no argument the webview is built with, and the webview_defaults.rs doc comment gains a blank line; both are clippy cleanups with no behaviour in them. The handler this edits is attached to the webview controller in setup and is unreachable from the renderer, so section 1's IPC surface is unchanged; the key it stops keeping is a browser accelerator, which no updater path reads.

[Pre-structure accumulation.] Everything below was recorded in the single free-text note field the ledger carried before acknowledgements became dated records, and it therefore runs several separate reviews together in one string. It is kept verbatim rather than split, because the per-review object ids and dates it would need were never recorded. It counts as one acknowledgement; the next one starts a fresh record. The commit this id records is the change the audit's own v1.2 revision describes, so the doc and the code were written against each other rather than the doc trailing the code. Recorded here rather than by bumping `Audited commit` because the SHA would name a pre-squash branch commit that stops existing on merge — the failure mode this ledger was built for. Diff read in full: the login flow gains a fourth fail-fast guard in OAuth2LoginService (granted scopes vs. the provider's required mail scopes, rejecting before persistence), OAuth2ClaimsExtractor gains requiredMailScopes(), and the Google and Microsoft extractors state theirs. The other four Code paths entries are untouched — verified as an empty diff for SecurityConfig.java, OAuth2CompletedStateTracker.java, ExternalProviderLoginService.java and resources/static, so PKCE, the state gate and the failure-redirect hygiene are byte-identical. Checked the three things that could have moved a verdict. (1) The check only ever rejects: it compares two sets and throws, it never adds a scope to a request, so the E-row claim that scopes are hardcoded in application.properties with no in-app escalation path still holds exactly. (2) It cannot resurrect a dead account — it runs before persistence and calls markRequiresReauthIfExists, the same direction as the refresh-token guard, so the flag is still cleared only by a login that is complete. (3) No token material reaches a log: the WARN line names the missing scope constants and a masked email, and the audit entry carries the same, so the log-hygiene claim in §2 is unchanged. Verdict stays PASS. 4d3f6d6 touches this path in comments only — verified by filtering the commit diff to lines that are neither comment nor blank, which comes back empty; the whole change is javadoc on OAuth2TokenService.exchangeRefreshToken. The old text claimed the method was used during the initial OAuth2 login flow, which no call site supports: ExternalProviderLoginService persists the refresh token and leaves the exchange to the first IMAP connection, by which point the account exists and the cached getAccessToken path applies. The method was deliberately kept rather than deleted, and precisely because of this boundary — it is the only route into doRefresh(accountId = null), so removing it would also make the accountId != null branch unreachable, and that branch is what invalidates the cached token and marks the account requires_reauth after a permanent refresh rejection, which the E row and the §2 log-hygiene claim both rest on. No executable line moves, so PKCE, the state gate, the granted-scope check added in v1.2, the failure-redirect hygiene and the masked-email logging are byte-identical. Whether to wire the method back up or collapse the nullable parameter is left as its own change with its own re-verification. Verdict stays PASS. Java caller gate batch: the only change under feature/auth is three javadoc lines adding the @callerless tag to OAuth2TokenService.exchangeRefreshToken, recording in machine-readable form the decision #299 already wrote out in prose — it is kept because deleting it would make the accountId != null guard in doRefresh unreachable, and that guard is what marks an account requires_reauth. No code line changed.

Comment-only change under this path. 578526c moves the @callerless waiver on OAuth2TokenService.exchangeRefreshToken out of javadoc into a line comment, because @callerless is not a javadoc tag and Error Prone rejected it with InvalidBlockTag. Verified line by line rather than by reading the intent: every added and removed line under this path is a comment line. What the waiver protects is untouched — exchangeRefreshToken still exists, and the accountId != null guard in doRefresh it keeps reachable, the guard that marks an account requires_reauth after a permanent rejection, is byte for byte the same. No token exchange, refresh path, scope, redirect URI, PKCE step or credential storage path moved. Verdict stays PASS.

One idiom change under this path. 7ec2793 rewrites both cache lookups in OAuth2TokenService.getAccessToken from "cached.isPresent() && cached.get().isFresh()" to tokenCache.get(accountId).filter(CachedToken::isFresh). Optional.filter evaluates the predicate only when a value is present, exactly as the && short-circuit did, and the cache is still read once per lookup, so the freshness decision, the double-check under the refresh lock and the fall-through to doRefresh all behave as before. No token is cached, logged or transmitted differently, and no scope, redirect URI or PKCE handling is in the diff. Verdict stays PASS.

Two paths, one change, and the second path is why this note is longer than its delta. In OAuth2TokenService.doRefresh, a permanent refresh rejection now publishes AccountRequiresReauthEvent after the updateRequiresReauth / updateLastError pair it already wrote, so a listener outside this feature can close the account's now-unreachable IMAP connections; the base constructor takes the publisher and the two subclasses pass it through. ExternalProviderLoginService.markRequiresReauthIfExists is the third writer of that flag and does the same, from TransactionCallbacks.runAfterCommit because it is @Transactional - the purge behind the event waits on the per-account connection lock, which must not be waited on with the single-writer SQLite transaction open, and before the commit the flag is not durable. Nothing about either token flow moves: the same permanent-vs-transient classification decides the branch, the refresh lock, the cache invalidate, the metric and the thrown MailOperationException are unchanged, the login path still writes exactly the credentials and account fields it did, and no scope, redirect URI, PKCE parameter, client secret or token value is read, logged or transmitted differently. The event is deliberately minimal for that reason - it carries the account id alone, so no token or address reaches a listener with no business holding either. Placement inside the existing try is checked by a mutation that moves it out: the flag is what makes the account unreachable, so an event published after a failed UPDATE would ask for live connections to be closed. Three mutations in total, each red on exactly the test that claims its rule, each verified to have reached the tests. Verdict stays PASS.

A count, not a token, moves. OAuth2TokenServiceRegistry.totalCachedTokens summed getCacheStats() per service, but every service holds the one TokenCache bean, so the diagnostic summary reported each cached token once per provider; the registry now takes the TokenCache and reads its size once, and the per-service getCacheStats/CacheStats, left without a caller, are removed. No token value, refresh path, cache key or invalidation changes, so no claim of this audit moves and the verdict stays PASS.

First note after the v1.9 re-verification, and it is the folder-move dropdown, not the rendering chain. The whole diff under this path is MessageMoveControl.svelte swapping its hand-written DropdownMenu.Portal + Content for the new MenuContent wrapper: same aria-label, same focus handler, same scroll variant, same align and sideOffset, now defaults inside the component instead of attributes at the call site. Checked rather than assumed: the element that renders message content is the iframe in MessageContent.svelte, which is not in this diff, and this control lists folder names from the folder store - it never receives message HTML. Nothing here touches the sandbox, the frame CSP, the sanitizer or the remote-image opt-in. Verdict stays PASS.

Second note after the v1.9 re-verification, and it is the keydown forwarder, not the isolation. The whole diff under this path is the preventDefault predicate inside MAIL_FRAME_SCRIPT, which stops cancelling browser defaults for combinations the app never claims (Ctrl+G, and the Shift variants of the claimed letters), plus the CSP hash that necessarily follows from changing the literal. Checked rather than assumed: the sandbox attributes, the opaque origin, the frame's default-src none, the sanitizer and the remote-image opt-in are byte-identical, and the postMessage payload the frame sends its parent is unchanged field for field - nothing new reaches the parent and nothing new is admitted into the frame. The hash is the one security-relevant line here, and it stays a pin on exactly one inline script: mailFrame.test.ts recomputes it from the literal, so it cannot drift from the script it authorises. Verdict stays PASS.

Third note after the v1.9 re-verification, and it is when the body takes focus, not what the body is. The whole diff under this path is MessageContent.svelte's focus effect calling the new shouldFocusBody rule instead of computing the intent inline, so that an intent naming another message stops reading as no intent at all. Checked rather than assumed: the iframe's sandbox attributes, its srcdoc assembly, the frame CSP, the sanitizer call and the remote-image opt-in are untouched, and no new value from the message reaches the DOM - the rule takes a stable id, a mode and a boolean, and returns a boolean. The only observable change is that the reading cursor stops being pulled into the frame when two navigations overlap. Verdict stays PASS.

Fourth note, and the smallest of the run. The whole diff under this path is one argument: MailContentService now names the IMAP lane it fetches a missing body on (Lane.INTERACTIVE) plus the import for it. Read in the tree rather than from the diff summary: getOrFetch is otherwise byte-identical — the same isBodyOversize short-circuit, the same MimePartExtractor.extractBody, the same escapePlainText for a text/plain part, the same referencedCids gate before collectInlineImages, the same HtmlSanitizer.sanitize call with the same inlineImages map, and the same IOException|RuntimeException wrap into MAIL_CONNECTION_ERROR. No sanitizer input, no cap, no branch and no persisted value moved. What the lane changes is which TCP connection the fetch travels on, which is a scheduling property; this boundary is about what happens to the bytes after they arrive, and that is untouched. Verdict stays PASS.

Printing a message reaches the body frame, read against sections 1, 2 and 3. No claim of this audit moves; verdict stays PASS. Two paths moved. (1) mailFrame.ts: the hash-pinned in-frame script gains two things. It cancels Ctrl+P alongside the keys it already claimed (the regex goes from /^[krfqu]$/i to /^[kprfqu]$/i), which is the same promise section 3 rests on for Ctrl+R and Ctrl+F -- the parent reacts to a synthetic replay, so only the frame can cancel the genuine event. And it measures its own document and posts the height out as __voxroxMailFrameHeight. That adds no capability: the frame already had window.parent.postMessage and has had it since the forwarder existed, so a body that got a script past the hash could always have posted anything it liked; what is new is that the parent listens for one more shape. It is validated on the same terms as the other two -- origin 'null' plus an exact source match to this frame's contentWindow in MessageContent.svelte, then isMailFrameHeightMessage, then clampMailFramePrintHeight, which rejects NaN, the infinities, zero and negatives and caps at 20000px. The height is applied to the iframe element between beforeprint and afterprint and restored afterwards, never to the pane on screen, so the worst a hostile height achieves is a print job up to about twenty A4 pages long that the user started themselves. Nothing about the sandbox, the frame CSP, img-src, the remote-image opt-in or the sanitizer is touched. Hashes recomputed independently rather than compared to a note, as this audit's own method section requires: MAIL_FRAME_SCRIPT 9DIi3Jm+1q0SAyuB5kl54K12o6ZiUBX8Zz8v6eITwTw= over 990 bytes and MAIL_FRAME_STYLE UXLUJbZ21yq1eqQCljjFZwc0mejRk10+TVL8FCWZ+C0= over 376 bytes, both matching the pinned constants, and mailFrame.test.ts pins them too. (2) components/message-detail: MessageContent.svelte gains the height branch described above and the beforeprint/afterprint pair, both removed on destroy; no sanitized HTML path, no new sink, and the body still never enters the app document.

Change under this path, read rather than waved through as a timing tweak. StartupTimingService swapped its reference clock: the anchor for processStartedAt and for every phase's startedAfterProcessMs moved from an Instant.now() taken in the class's own static initialiser to ManagementFactory.getRuntimeMXBean().getStartTime(), with a wall-clock constant recording how much boot had already passed when the class loaded. Section 1 is untouched by it: the diff does not enter StorageContextInitializer, reads or writes no crypto.bin, touches neither the VOXSEC1 format, the DPAPI USER-scope call, the buffer zeroing, the atomic private-permissioned write, nor the constant-time crypto.fingerprint comparison, and adds no path by which any of them could be reached earlier or skipped. The class holds no secret and opens no file. Section 2 holds: CryptoService is not in the diff, and the one place where boot timing and that section intersect - the self-test "warmed off the boot path" claim - is about when the self-test runs, which this change does not move; it only changes what a later dump reports about the time that had already elapsed. The new dependency is java.management, read-only and already in the sidecar's --add-modules list; it is an MXBean read, not a JNI or FFM call, so the "pure Java FFM (no JNI)" hygiene claim of section 1 is about a path this does not join. Section 3 residuals are unaffected - nothing about mail.db plaintext at rest or the same-user-malware exclusion turns on a clock source. The one observable effect outside the boundary is that startup-timings.json in the diagnostic dump now reports a start roughly four seconds earlier and correspondingly larger phase offsets: the same data category as before, no new field and no new value class, and the dump's privacy check is RELEASE_CHECKLIST section 7, which is flagged for a re-take on this candidate for exactly this reason.

The sync open gains a CONDSTORE step, read against sections 1 and 2. No claim of this audit moves; verdict stays PASS. Four files moved, all on the sync path. ImapFolderExecutor: executeReadOnlyResynced, still the sync cycle's only entry, now opens QRESYNC when there is a baseline, else IMAPFolder.open(mode, ResyncData.CONDSTORE) where the server advertises CONDSTORE and ENABLE, else plain, each failure degrading to the next exactly as the QRESYNC failure did at 1.7; executeReadOnly and executeReadWrite share one opener that calls folder.open(mode) and nothing else, which ImapFolderExecutorTest now pins for the read-only one. On the wire that is ENABLE CONDSTORE plus EXAMINE with the CONDSTORE parameter, and the server's answer adds one number, HIGHESTMODSEQ, plus a MODSEQ item on later untagged FETCH responses of that connection; both are parsed by Angus, and the second was already reachable, since the QRESYNC open 1.7 describes enables CONDSTORE implicitly. ImapCapabilities additionally reads ENABLE from the same post-auth capability list. FlagSyncService and MailSyncService change only which HIGHESTMODSEQ they store and resume from: a non-positive one is neither stored nor sent, and a stored -1 is read as no baseline. A hostile server can therefore choose the number it is asked to resynchronize from next time, which is less than the section 2 QRESYNC bullet already grants it; the vanished-UID delete, its (account, folder) scope and its batching are byte-identical. A rejected ENABLE or SELECT makes Angus log that pooled connection out, the same Angus-internal path a rejected QRESYNC open already took; ImapConnectionManager is untouched, so the section 1 claims (checkserveridentity, the XOAUTH2 TLS requirement, the per-lane pool and locks) stand as written. MessageFetcher, MailContentService, MimePartExtractor and the fetch profile are untouched, so sections 2 to 4b are unaffected.

One log line in ThreadingService drops the thread root Message-ID; the diff against the previous reviewed tree is that line and its comment. No claim of this audit moves, verdict stays PASS: the audit makes no claim about what the sync path logs, and removing a logged value changes no protocol handling, fetch profile or bound.

A constant becomes a setting. UidEnumerationSchedule takes its interval from the new SyncProperties.uidEnumerationInterval (mail.client.sync.uid-enumeration-interval, default 1h, the value the constant held) through an @Autowired constructor; the test constructor with an injected clock is unchanged. Nothing about what the enumeration fetches or how the server is trusted moves, the default cadence is the same, and only the soak profile shortens it, so no claim of this audit moves and the verdict stays PASS.
